# Cloud Markdown↔ADF functions (pure capability; AdfCodec untouched)

## Context / Problem
Jira Cloud stores rich text as ADF (structured JSON). The `RichTextCodec` seam
(epic e369, story J3) routes Cloud rich text through `AdfCodec`
(`adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`), a pass-through over the pinned
`adapters/jira/adf.py`. **`adf.py`'s encode is plain-text-structured, not
Markdown-aware:** `text_to_adf` (`adf.py:275`) splits on blank lines and emits each
block as one `paragraph`, so headings, list markers, fenced code and inline
bold/strike/link are carried as **literal characters** and Cloud renders raw
source. `adf_to_text` (`adf.py:26`) already emits Markdown-ish text on decode; the
missing half is a Markdown-aware **encode**.

**Why this story ships pure functions, not a codec change.** On Cloud the codec ops
are reachable on the LIVE send path (`AdfCodec.fit_outbound` fits the posted
description; the compare sites call `adf.py` directly). Repointing `AdfCodec` here
would change live truncation and comparison — a cutover that must land together
with echo-safety in story 3388. So **this story adds the Markdown↔ADF functions and
their tests, and leaves `AdfCodec` a plain pass-through**
(`rich_text_codec.py:25/29/33/37`). Nothing observable changes on merge.

## Engine: marklas as an OPTIONAL EXTRA, lazily imported (not vendored)
`marklas` (pure-Python, mistune-based; `github.com/byExist/marklas`) pinned EXACTLY
at **0.8.6** as a new optional extra together with its transitive `mistune` 3.3.4.
The pin is exact because this story depends on a specific API surface — encode
`marklas.to_adf`, decode `marklas.to_md` — and on measured output shape. Licences:
marklas is **MIT**, mistune is **BSD-3-Clause** (both OSI-approved, both
permissive); the extra records each.

**Superseded plan + deviation record.** The earlier plan vendored marklas under
`src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/`. A plan review BLOCKed that: marklas needs `mistune`,
the engine importing `adf.py` is contractually dependency-free (`pyproject.toml:69`),
and `src/rebar/_vendor/` is not importable from the reconciler subprocess. Chosen
instead: **lazy-import inside the three function bodies, with `ImportError` routed
to the plain-text `adf.py` fallback** — preserving the stdlib-only contract and
mirroring the `agents`/`metrics`/`grounding` extras. Vendoring stays available
later; this is the deviation record. The "tolerate a no-extras install"
requirement belongs to story 3388's cutover and is recorded there.

## Measured evidence (re-measured here; the prior figures did not survive)
The prior plan quoted a 2026-08-03 export and `files/parity_*.py` artifacts. **None
of that survives** — not on disk, not in git history; rebar has no attachment store.
Re-measured against the live store (4,996 unique bodies): idempotence **reproduces**
(99.65% claimed vs 99.75% measured); the "5,730 bodies" cardinality is **stale**; and
structural richness does **NOT** reproduce (56.7% claimed vs 20.5% measured).
AC bars are set from the committed fixture, not from the claims.

**Richness predicate (explicit):** a body is structurally rich iff its encoded ADF
contains at least one non-paragraph BLOCK node — `heading`, `bulletList`,
`orderedList`, `codeBlock`, `taskList`, `blockquote`, `rule`, `table` or `panel`.
Inline marks alone do NOT qualify (that looser predicate yields 25.2%).

A full corpus cannot be committed: `check-added-large-files` caps files at 500 KB,
there is no LFS, and `.gitignore` records a decision not to raise it. The fixture is
a scrubbed, sharded sample from a committed generator, mirroring
`scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py` doctrine.

## Two defects the functions must handle (both reproduced here)
1. **Combined-mark 2-cycle.** `A **~~both~~** end` ⇄ `A ~~**both**~~ end` alternates
   forever under repeated round-trip — an exact 2-cycle. A deterministic
   **mark-order canonicalizer** in `adf_to_markdown` is required.
2. **HTML comments are dropped.** marklas removes them: `text <!-- x --> more`
   becomes `text  more`, and a lone marker becomes the empty string. rebar's own
   reconciler echo marker is an HTML comment. 8 of 4,996 live bodies carry one and
   3 of the first 8 lose it. **Mechanism:** `markdown_to_adf` self-verifies — it
   decodes its own result and, if any `<!-- … -->` present in the source is missing,
   returns the plain `text_to_adf(md)` encode for that body instead — so an engine
   quirk degrades richness rather than losing content. Exactly 1 of the 360
   committed corpus bodies carries an HTML comment, and it loses that comment
   without this mechanism.

## Approach (pure functions in `adf.py`)
Add three functions, **not referenced by any `AdfCodec` op or live send path here**:
1. `markdown_to_adf(md) -> dict` — Markdown-aware encode via `marklas.to_adf`, with
   the HTML-comment self-verification above.
2. `adf_to_markdown(doc) -> str` — decode via `marklas.to_md`, applying the
   mark-order canonicalizer.
3. `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit(md, *, limit=…) -> str` — length-fit measuring the
   `markdown_to_adf` serialization.
Plus a whole-codec **plain-text fallback helper** returning the existing plain
`adf.py` functions as a set, which 3388 installs on conversion error — defined and
unit-tested here, wired there. Existing plain functions stay untouched.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira/adf.py` — the three functions + canonicalizer + fallback helper.
- `pyproject.toml` — pinned optional extra (marklas + mistune); `src/rebar/_optional.py`
  — register it.
- `scripts/build_cloud_adf_corpus.py` (new) + `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/` (new).
- **UNCHANGED:** `AdfCodec` and its four ops; the shared plain-text
  `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`; every live Cloud send/compare site.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `adf.markdown_to_adf` emits Markdown-aware ADF nodes (heading/list/code plus
  inline marks) rather than literal `#`/`-`/`**`; verified by
  `test_cloud_adf_roundtrip` asserting node types.
- [ ] `adf.adf_to_markdown` returns the source Markdown for a structured body;
  verified by `test_cloud_adf_roundtrip` asserting decoded equality.
- [ ] The combined strong+strikethrough 2-cycle is eliminated by the mark-order
  canonicalizer; verified by `test_cloud_mark_order_converges` pinning the measured
  `**~~x~~**` ⇄ `~~**x**~~` oscillation as a regression.
- [ ] An HTML comment present in the source survives the round-trip, falling back to
  the plain encode when the engine would drop it; verified by
  `test_cloud_html_comment_survives`.
- [ ] `adf.fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` measures the `markdown_to_adf` serialization
  rather than the plain encode; verified by
  `test_adf_fit_measures_the_serialized_document_not_the_plain_text`.
- [ ] With marklas absent, importing `adf` succeeds and each of the three functions
  returns its plain-`adf.py` result rather than raising; verified by
  `test_cloud_functions_degrade_without_marklas` simulating the ImportError.
- [ ] The plain-text fallback helper returns the existing plain `adf.py` functions
  as a set; verified by `test_cloud_plain_fallback_helper_returns_plain_functions`.
- [ ] Over the committed `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/`, the MD→ADF→MD
  round-trip reaches a fixed point after one pass for ≥99.6% of bodies (measured
  100.00% over 360 bodies, 0 conversion errors); verified by
  `test_cloud_corpus_idempotence`.
- [ ] Over the same fixture, ≥15% of bodies encode to structurally rich ADF under
  the block-node predicate defined above (measured 15.6%); verified by
  `test_cloud_corpus_richness`.
- [ ] The committed fixture cardinality is pinned at 360 bodies, so a silent
  regeneration fails; verified by `test_cloud_corpus_cardinality_is_pinned`.
- [ ] The committed fixture carries no unscrubbed emails, tenant hostnames or URLs;
  verified by `test_cloud_corpus_carries_no_unscrubbed_secrets`.
- [ ] `AdfCodec` and its four ops remain a plain pass-through; verified by the
  existing `test_adf_codec_is_a_pass_through_to_the_pinned_adf_module` staying green
  unmodified.
